- Model consistently underestimates late-period price spikes (especially after 10–15 day horizon), particularly in the 20–30 day forecast window.
- Forecasts show early mean reversion bias — overcorrecting downward after initial spikes, then failing to capture subsequent upward momentum.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits strong underestimation bias, especially in the 15–30 day range.
- Overshoots occur after sharp upward moves in history (e.g., 77.73 → 80.03), leading to over-optimistic 30d forecasts that fail to account for volatility decay.
- Model tends to ignore recent high volatility periods in history, underweighting them in 30d forecasts despite strong momentum.
- If true outcome shows a sharp drop after a spike, model often fails to adjust downward — suggesting lag in recognizing reversal signals.
- Forecasts should be adjusted upward by 2–5% if recent 7–14 day history shows sustained upward momentum, even if sentiment is neutral.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% in 15–30 day window, model should be re-calibrated to include a 3–5 day lagged momentum buffer.
